skill.name: writing-shape
skill.description: Shape raw markdown material into a structured article through a paragraph-by-paragraph writing session.
skill.summary: Turns fixed source material into a coherent article draft with explicit structure and grounding.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by prose and markdown examples in SKILL.md. I found no evidence of shell execution, system reconnaissance, prompt injection, or data exfiltration intent.

static_findings.snippet: - **Inline vs. callout.** Tips, warnings, and asides go in callouts (`> [!TIP]`, `> [!NOTE]`) — but
If the user did not say where to save the article, ask once and remember the path.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 64 uses markdown inline backticks to show callout syntax, not Ruby or shell execution. There is no executable code or command invocation.
Line 13 asks the user for an article save path when none is provided. This is normal output-file selection, not system reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Raw notes and transcripts often lack a clear argument. This skill turns fixed source material into a structured article, one paragraph at a time.
actual_capabilities: Reads a user-provided markdown source file before drafting.
Defines audience prerequisites before selecting an article opening.
Drafts two or three opening options for user selection.
Builds the article paragraph by paragraph with user approval.
Tracks grounded concepts so later sections do not outrun the reader.
Chooses between prose, lists, tables, callouts, quotes, and code blocks.
limitations: Does not edit the raw material file.
Does not create new source material without user input.
Does not publish articles or add platform formatting by default.
Requires user decisions throughout the drafting session.

use_cases.title: Convert Research Notes
use_cases.description: Turn a markdown pile of notes, fragments, and quotes into a coherent article draft.

use_cases.title: Structure Transcript Material
use_cases.description: Shape interview or talk transcripts into an argument with clear prerequisites and grounded concepts.

use_cases.title: Refine Draft Direction
use_cases.description: Test multiple openings, choose an angle, and grow the article with explicit editorial tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Start From Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Shape my notes into an article. Read notes.md, ask where to save the article, and propose three openings.

prompt_templates.title: Set Reader Prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-shape process on research.md. Set prerequisites for a beginner developer audience, then draft candidate openings.

prompt_templates.title: Build With Grounding
prompt_templates.prompt: Shape transcript.md into a technical blog post. Keep a grounded concepts list and challenge weak transitions before appending each block.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Formats Deliberately
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a full shaping session for essay-notes.md. Compare prose, lists, tables, callouts, quotes, and code blocks before each major section.

output_examples.input: Raw notes about API versioning and migration risk.
output: Three candidate openings with different angles.
A selected article path and first approved paragraph.
A grounded concept list for later sections.

output_examples.input: Transcript fragments from a developer talk about testing.
output: A structured article draft that starts from the audience prerequisite.
Paragraphs appended after each editorial decision.
Notes about missing examples that the user must provide or cut.

output_examples.input: Existing draft that drifts away from its opening promise.
output_examples.output: A revised sequence that either re-threads the argument or changes the opening before more paragraphs are added.

best_practices: Provide one markdown file with the fixed source material.
Decide the reader prerequisites before choosing an opening.
Review each paragraph before the skill appends the next block.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to invent evidence missing from the source material.
Do not use it for final platform publishing without a separate review.
Do not skip the opening selection step when the article direction is unclear.

faq.question: What type of input works best?
faq.answer: A markdown file with notes, fragments, transcript text, or rough prose works best.

faq.question: Does it edit the raw material?
faq.answer: No. The skill treats the raw material as read-only and writes a separate article document.

faq.question: Can it create new examples?
faq.answer: It names gaps and asks for missing examples instead of inventing source material.

faq.question: How does it choose structure?
faq.answer: It discusses each block format with the user, including prose, lists, tables, callouts, quotes, and code blocks.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it for final publishing?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on article shaping, not platform formatting, frontmatter, or publishing.
